title: The best Voice AI for Italian Restaurants
summary: Find the best voice AI for Italian restaurants. See how Certus AI handles phone orders, reservations, and catering calls automatically, with direct POS integration and zero missed calls.
body_markdown:
Italian restaurants run on hospitality. The whole point is that guests feel welcomed, fed well, and taken care of.


But that reputation takes a hit every time a call goes unanswered, a catering inquiry disappears into a voicemail nobody checks, or a family has to find another spot because nobody picked up.


The phone has always been a weak link in Italian restaurant operations. The food is made with care. The dining room runs on personality. And the phone gets answered when someone happens to be free, which during a busy service, is almost never.


[Restaurant voice AI](https://www.certus-ai.com/) is changing that for Italian restaurants across North America. This post covers what it is, why it fits this type of operation particularly well, and what to look for when choosing the right system.


‍


## TLDR


Voice AI for Italian restaurants answers every inbound call automatically, takes phone orders with full accuracy, books reservations, and handles customer questions around the clock. For trattorias, pizzerias, and Italian-American casual dining spots, where phone orders and reservation calls are high volume and high stakes, this technology directly recovers missed revenue without adding staff.


Certus AI is purpose-built for this use case, with POS integration, English and Spanish support, and same-day setup.


‍


## How Italian restaurants lose revenue on the phone


According to[IBISWorld's 2025 Italian Restaurants industry report](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/italian-restaurants/4303/) , the Italian restaurant industry in the United States reached an estimated $112.4 billion in revenue in 2025, growing at a CAGR of 5.8% over the past five years. There are nearly 45,000 Italian restaurants operating in the US right now. Competition is real, margins are tight, and every order matters.


The phone is where a surprising amount of that revenue leaks. Italian restaurants tend to have higher average checks than fast casual, stronger demand for group bookings and family-style catering orders, and regulars who prefer to call. That combination makes missed calls more expensive than in almost any other restaurant format.


Frank, the owner of Baci Trattoria & Pizza in Naples, FL, put it plainly: "At the end of the night I'd say, I lost about six, seven phone calls. And maybe one of those could have been $200. Maybe a party of 20 people. You don't know."


Before he adopted Certus AI, Frank was running five separate phone lines at Baci. Green lights flashing in the kitchen, calls stacking up at the front, and an automated hold message that most callers ignored before hanging up. On the busiest nights, he'd take the phone off the hook entirely. Just because there was no other way to get through service.


‍


## How can voice AI for Italian restaurants help?


An[AI phone agent for restaurants](https://www.certus-ai.com/) answers every inbound call the moment it comes in. No rings going unanswered. No hold music. No staff member pulling away from a table to deal with the phone.


Here is what the system handles from start to finish:


- **Phone order taking:** The AI knows your full menu, including every modification, topping, pasta preparation, and dietary request. It takes the order, confirms it with the caller, and sends it directly to your POS.
- **Reservation booking:** It checks real-time availability, books the table, collects the guest's name and contact details, and confirms the reservation automatically.
- **Catering and group inquiries:** Large party calls get captured and routed correctly rather than dropped during a busy service.
- **Customer questions:** Hours, parking, allergen information, delivery zones, specials. The AI answers instantly without needing a staff member.
- **Bilingual support:** For Italian restaurants serving diverse communities, the AI handles calls in English and Spanish without needing bilingual staff on the floor.


At Baci, Certus AI's voicebot is named Tony. Frank's regulars are older and have always asked for Tony or Frank when they call. So he gave the AI a familiar name, and now his regulars call in, place their orders, and come to pick them up. As Frank put it: "A lot of people don't even know they're talking to a robot. They come in and say, 'Oh, Tony took my order.'"


‍

It knows that "a party of twelve on Saturday" means a reservation call, not an order. It knows your specific preparation terms, your ingredient names, and your kitchen instructions.

## How does restaurant voice AI integration with POS work?


This is one of the most important questions to ask any voice AI provider before committing. Without POS integration, the AI is just taking a message. With it, the AI completes the order from start to finish.


When[restaurant voice AI integration with POS](https://www.certus-ai.com/) works correctly, the flow looks like this:


1. Customer calls and the AI answers immediately
2. The AI takes the full order, including modifications and special instructions
3. The order is confirmed verbally with the caller
4. The order fires directly into your POS as if a staff member had entered it
5. The kitchen receives it and starts prep


No one on your team touches the phone. No one re-enters the order. The caller gets a confirmation. The kitchen gets the ticket. Frank described cutting from five phone lines down to one as a direct result of this. The cost reduction on his phone bill alone went from $700 a month to $350. That was before accounting for the recovered revenue.


For Italian restaurants running on Square POS specifically, the integration works out of the box with Certus. For a comparison of voice AI options across different POS systems, see our post on[AI voice assistants for pizza shop orders](https://www.certus-ai.com/blogs/best-ai-voice-assistants-for-pizza-shop-orders) , which covers the POS compatibility question in detail.

## Is a restaurant answering service worth it for Italian restaurants?


For a trattoria or Italian-American spot with consistent phone volume, the answer is almost always yes. Here's why:


If your restaurant misses an average of five calls per service, and each missed call represents a $60 order, that is $300 in lost revenue per shift. Over a month of dinner service, that is roughly $9,000 walking out the door through an unanswered phone.


A[restaurant answering service](https://www.certus-ai.com/) built on voice AI captures those calls at a fraction of that cost.


The cost of missed calls also compounds in ways that are harder to measure. A catering client who can't reach you books somewhere else and may never call back. A regular who hits voicemail twice in a row starts ordering online from a competitor. The phone is often the first point of contact for high-value customers, and a missed call is a missed relationship.


For more on how to evaluate whether the ROI makes sense for your specific operation, see our post on[whether a restaurant answering service is worth it](https://www.certus-ai.com/blogs/is-a-restaurant-answering-service-worth-it) .

## What happens to staff when an AI handles the phones?


This is worth addressing directly, because it comes up with almost every restaurant owner who is considering the switch.


The AI does not replace your team. It handles the one task your team cannot do well during service: answering the phone while simultaneously doing everything else. Your servers stay on the floor. Your host manages the dining room. Your kitchen runs cleaner tickets with fewer errors because the AI never mishears an order or forgets a modification.


Frank put it clearly after implementing Certus at Baci: "Never takes a day off. She works around the clock from 10 o'clock to 9 and she doesn't complain. A human person cannot answer five lines at the same time. This program can. Employee of the month, she's the best."


His staff saved over 130 hours in a single period that would have previously been spent managing phone calls. That time went back into the dining room, into prep, and into the kind of hospitality that Italian restaurants are built on.

The global Italian restaurant market was valued at $212.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $348.6 billion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 5.7%. The operators who scale within that market will not do it by hiring more people to answer phones. They will do it by building systems that handle volume without adding headcount.


Frank's expansion plan makes the point better than any statistic. Baci is opening a second location in September 2026. His first infrastructure decision for the new site was not the POS, the kitchen layout, or the reservation system. It was the phone. "By September we're opening another location. The first thing is the phone system. The first thing that will get built is Tony."


That is what[restaurant AI technology](https://www.certus-ai.com/) looks like when it works. Not a pilot program or an experiment. A core piece of infrastructure that gets replicated before anything else.
